acceptedClaims.statement:
The committed `coloring.csv` is a complete six-coloring of
`{1, 2, ..., 536}` with no monochromatic solution to `x + y = z`, including
the case `x = y`. It therefore independently replays the published baseline
lower bound

```text
S(6) >= 536.
```

This certificate does not improve the bound. The problem's published interval
remains `536 <= S(6) <= 1836`.
acceptedClaims.validitySummary: The audited artifacts establish that `coloring.csv` assigns exactly one of six colors to every integer from 1 through 536 and contains no monochromatic solution to x+y=z, including x=y. The verifier exhaustively checks all 71,824 relevant ordered representatives with 1≤x≤y and x+y≤536. This proves S(6)≥536.
scopeQualifications: The certificate provides no coloring beyond 536 and therefore does not improve the lower bound.
It contains no upper-bound argument; the supplied published interval remains 536≤S(6)≤1836.

value.title: Canonical encodings of the Fredricksen–Sweet 536-coloring witness
value.summary: `coloring.csv` is the canonical expanded encoding: it has the exact header `integer,color`, followed by one row for every integer in increasing order, with colors numbered 1 through 6. `published-symmetric.json` preserves the compact form printed by the source paper. Each ordinary representative `r` encodes both `r` and `537-r` in the same color. The exceptional pair is recorded explicitly as `[179, 4]` and `[358, 1]`.

value.title: Explicit six-coloring of {1,...,536}
value.summary:
The committed `coloring.csv` is a complete six-coloring of
`{1, 2, ..., 536}` with no monochromatic solution to `x + y = z`, including
the case `x = y`.

value.title: Exact checker for the Fredricksen–Sweet 536-coloring
value.summary: The pinned Python-standard-library checker validates the compact witness schema, expands it with exact coverage of `1..536`, validates the canonical CSV and its exact agreement with the compact witness, and enumerates all 71,824 in-range triples with `1 <= x <= y` and `x + y <= 536`, including `x = y`. It is replayed with `python3 -I -B verify.py published-symmetric.json coloring.csv`.

value.title: Exhaustive certificate proof for the 536-coloring
value.summary: The audited artifacts establish that `coloring.csv` assigns exactly one of six colors to every integer from 1 through 536 and contains no monochromatic solution to `x+y=z`, including `x=y`. The verifier exhaustively checks all 71,824 relevant ordered representatives with `1≤x≤y` and `x+y≤536`.

value.title: Published baseline lower bound S(6) ≥ 536
value.summary:
It therefore independently replays the published baseline lower bound

```text
S(6) >= 536.
```

This certificate does not improve the bound. The problem's published interval
remains `536 <= S(6) <= 1836`.
